target.objective: an accurate title-thumbnail promise that earns both the click and continued viewing

platform_contract.notes: YouTube's current native experiment can test titles, thumbnails, or their combinations and chooses by watch time. This supersedes the repository packaging skill's thumbnail-only assumption; implementation must feature-detect or version the contract.

evidence_levels.observational_research: Quantitative association; not causal proof for a channel.
evidence_levels.practice_consensus: Recurring professional pattern that needs channel calibration.
evidence_levels.case_observation: Directly observed in the cited channel sample; intention and effect remain unproven.

patterns.name: Title and thumbnail as one promise
patterns.use: Assign each component a distinct job: the title names the subject/value with enough context; the image and short overlay add a visual claim, tension, relationship, or interpretation.
avoid: a thumbnail beat absent from the video

patterns.name: Search-readable title
patterns.use: Place the most important accurate entities and topic phrases early enough to survive truncation; state what happened, what is analyzed, or what the viewer will learn.
avoid: burying the main entity after branding

patterns.name: Browse-oriented intrigue title
patterns.use: Frame a truthful tension, consequence, contrast, or unanswered question while retaining a specific noun or event.
avoid: sensational implication unsupported by the video

patterns.name: Stable channel-recognition template
patterns.use: Hold a small set of stable tokens—type family, text zone, creator/logo anchor, border/accent behavior, and compositional rhythm—while changing the story image and hook.
avoid: brand marks larger than the story

patterns.name: Topic-specific hero subject
patterns.use: Give the person, object, place, or evidence central to this story most of the visual area.
avoid: a creator face unrelated to the specific story

patterns.name: Small creator signature inset
patterns.use: Use a consistent, subordinate creator portrait as a channel signature when the story subject—not the host—should dominate.
avoid: forcing a face when it consumes needed semantic space

patterns.name: Short interpretive overlay
patterns.use: Add a brief phrase, label, metaphor, or pun that interprets the story rather than restating the full title.
avoid: a joke that distorts a serious claim

patterns.name: Consistent high-contrast text zone
patterns.use: Reserve a predictable region with strong foreground/background separation and a readable type family.

patterns.name: Controlled template evolution
patterns.use: Version templates deliberately: retain enough signature tokens to remain recognizable while testing a meaningful change in hierarchy, imagery, or text treatment.
avoid: simultaneous changes that cannot be interpreted
treating brand consistency as immunity from testing

patterns.name: Three genuinely different packaging hypotheses
patterns.use: Test up to three distinct title, thumbnail, or pair hypotheses whose differences are large enough to answer a question.
avoid: three colorways of the same concept
calling an inconclusive result a winner

patterns.name: Honest curiosity and dignity
patterns.use: Create interest through real tension and specificity without inventing evidence, overstating guilt, demeaning subjects, or promising a beat the video does not contain.

sample.note: Counts describe the current loaded grid at inspection time; they do not establish performance causality.

direct_observations: Current thumbnails repeatedly use a black upper-left text block with large condensed white uppercase lettering.
The central/right field is dominated by story-specific people, objects, places, or a small collage.
A small, consistent Dr. Grande portrait appears near the upper-right as an authorship signature while the story subject remains dominant.
A small DR. GRANDE wordmark appears near the lower-left.

Overlay phrases are usually compact interpretive hooks or puns such as AFFAIR ON RETAINER, ROO THE DAY, CLOSING TIME, DEGREE OF DECEPTION, and TRASH TALK; they complement rather than reproduce the long descriptive title.
Current titles heavily use named entities, roles/relationships, concrete actions, consequences, and sometimes an Analysis/Update suffix.
The popular grid includes an older template centered on Dr. Grande, with a bottom brand strip and different text treatment, showing recognizable brand evolution rather than one immutable layout.
inferences: The repeated corner anchors and typography likely enable pre-reading channel recognition.
The long title performs much of the search/relevance work, while the thumbnail performs rapid recognition, story identification, and interpretive intrigue.
A subordinate creator inset can preserve channel identity without displacing the case subject.
cannot_conclude: The template caused any video's view count.
The title length or Analysis suffix is optimal for another channel.
A face, black text block, pun, or fixed corner placement universally improves CTR or watch time.
The creator's intended keyword strategy without channel-side analytics or an interview.
